facts.value: The library once had a 200-foot tower, the tallest structure in Madras at the time. It was pulled down in March 1897 because it was unsafe.
facts.quote: The library had an imposing tower 200 feet high, the highest in Madras at that time. But in March 1897 AD, the tower was demolished

facts.value: The site was once the Pantheon, also known as the Public Rooms or Assembly Rooms, where the elite of the city met. In 1821 it was sold to E.S. Moorat, an Armenian merchant, who sold it back to the Government in 1830 for Rs 28,000.
facts.quote: sold the main house and central garden space to E.S. Moorat, a wealthy Armenian merchant, who in turn, sold it back to the Government in 1830 AD, for Rs.28,000
